chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a slave who is owned by partners, if one of them sells his share, the other partner says, 'I have more right to it.' Is that so? He said, 'Yes, if there is only one [other partner].' Then it was said to him, 'Is there pre-emption in animals?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal to buy a share when another sells)

ai.seo_question: Does the right of pre-emption apply to animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the scope of pre-emption (*shuf'ah*) by distinguishing between human slaves and animals, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding property rights. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the right for slaves, reflecting the high social and economic status of slaves in early Islamic society, while explicitly excluding animals, thereby limiting the application of *shuf'ah* to specific categories of movable property. This ruling underscores the principle that legal rights are contingent upon the nature of the asset and the context of shared ownership.
